data_objects.name: cyclone_observation_metadata
data_objects.meaning: A row-level index of timestamped cyclone observations from 2020 through 2024, including event coordinates and attributes plus a relative path intended to link each row to an HDF5 infrared image.

data_objects.name: infrared_brightness_temperature_rasters
data_objects.meaning: A directory collection of event-partitioned HDF5 files. Each inspected file contains one 512 by 512 floating-point raster named Infrared whose attributes identify it as brightness temperature in kelvin.

variables.name: year
variables.meaning: Year component of the observation timestamp.

variables.name: month
variables.meaning: Month component of the observation timestamp.

variables.name: day
variables.meaning: Day-of-month component of the observation timestamp.

variables.name: hour
variables.meaning: Hour component of the observation timestamp; the time zone is not stated in the public artifacts.

variables.name: grade
variables.meaning: Categorical cyclone grade code recorded for the observation; observed codes are 0, 2, 3, 4, and 5, but no code legend is present.

variables.name: lat
variables.meaning: Latitude coordinate recorded for the cyclone observation; the coordinate unit and datum are not explicitly declared.

variables.name: lng
variables.meaning: Longitude coordinate recorded for the cyclone observation; the coordinate convention, unit, and datum are not explicitly declared.

variables.name: pressure
variables.meaning: Pressure value associated with the cyclone observation; the precise pressure definition and unit are not stated.

variables.name: wind
variables.meaning: Wind value associated with the cyclone observation; the measurement definition and unit are not stated.

variables.name: dir50
variables.meaning: Direction-code field associated with the level labeled 50; all public rows contain 9 and the code meaning is not defined.

variables.name: long50
variables.meaning: Long-dimension field associated with the level labeled 50; all public rows contain zero and its physical interpretation is not defined.

variables.name: short50
variables.meaning: Short-dimension field associated with the level labeled 50; all public rows contain zero and its physical interpretation is not defined.

variables.name: dir30
variables.meaning: Direction-code field associated with the level labeled 30; all public rows contain 9 and the code meaning is not defined.

variables.name: long30
variables.meaning: Long-dimension field associated with the level labeled 30; all public rows contain zero and its physical interpretation is not defined.

variables.name: short30
variables.meaning: Short-dimension field associated with the level labeled 30; all public rows contain zero and its physical interpretation is not defined.

variables.name: landfall
variables.meaning: Landfall indicator field; every public row has value zero, and the encoding is otherwise undocumented.

variables.name: intp
variables.meaning: Binary field named intp with observed values 0 and 1; its name suggests interpolation, but the exact condition represented by the flag is not stated.

variables.name: mask
variables.meaning: Pixel-count quantity associated with masking of the linked raster. In inspected nonzero rows it equals mask_pct multiplied by the 512 by 512 pixel count, apart from decimal rounding; the mask criterion is not stated.

variables.name: mask_pct
variables.meaning: Fraction of raster pixels associated with mask; despite the pct suffix, observed values are fractional proportions and agree with mask divided by 512 by 512, subject to rounding.

variables.name: id
variables.meaning: Cyclone event identifier used to partition the image directory and repeated in image filenames.

variables.name: hdf_full_path
variables.meaning: Relative path intended to identify the HDF5 image for the metadata row.

variables.name: Infrared
variables.meaning: The sole root dataset found in each representative HDF5 file: a 512 by 512 float64 brightness-temperature raster. Dataset attributes are long_name=Brightness temperature and units=K (kelvin).

structure.description: Each metadata row represents one hourly timestamp for one cyclone ID. Concatenating year, month, day, and hour produces the leading YYYYMMDDHH token found in its declared HDF5 filename.
Image files are partitioned under directories named by cyclone ID. Observed filenames follow a timestamp-ID-HMW8-or-HMW9-1 pattern, and hdf_full_path is the table-to-file linkage key.

The public table has 10,347 unique declared image paths across 58 cyclone IDs, while the image directory contains 8,279 HDF5 files across 47 IDs. Every present HDF5 file is declared by exactly one metadata row, but 2,068 declared paths belonging to 11 IDs are absent from the public image directory.
Three representative HMW8 and HMW9 files from 2021 through 2023 share the same sampled schema: one zlib-compressed, chunked, 512 by 512 float64 Infrared array with brightness-temperature attributes.

uncertainties: No in-scope data dictionary defines the grade codes, pressure and wind conventions or units, the 30/50 field family, the landfall encoding, or the intp and mask generation rules.
The timestamp time zone is not specified.
The longitude convention is not stated; observed lng values extend above 180, up to 212.1.

The sampled HDF5 files contain no coordinate arrays or declared spatial bounds, coordinate reference system, pixel size, or axis orientation, so the raster georegistration cannot be established from the public artifacts alone.
The meanings of the HMW8 and HMW9 filename tokens and the trailing 1 token are not declared in the inspected artifacts.
The public artifacts do not state why 2,068 paths declared in the metadata table are missing from the image directory or whether those omissions are intentional.

Only three representative HDF5 files, spanning both observed HMW tokens and years 2021 through 2023, were used as structural schema evidence; schema consistency outside that sample was not exhaustively verified.
annotation_notes: Inspection was restricted to the public root containing combined_metadata_2020_to_2024.csv and image_2020_to_2024.
The CSV header, boundary rows, whole-table counts and value domains, path inventory, and representative nonzero mask rows were inspected.

Three representative HDF5 files were used for schema inspection: two HMW8 files and one HMW9 file spanning 2021, 2022, and 2023. All three exposed the same root dataset name, shape, numeric type, and semantic attributes.
Units remain null in the normalized variable records because the JSON schema requests null unit fields; explicit or missing unit information is retained in each variable meaning.
